problems.nature: phishing and social engineering via crafted email content
problems.description: This problem involves detecting phishing and social engineering attacks embedded in email content characterized by text-heavy narratives, obfuscated email addresses, suspicious URLs, and varied linguistic styles. Attackers exploit emotional manipulation through financial gain or health-related lures, using domain spoofing and URL obfuscation to evade detection. The detection complexity is moderate to high due to multi-source data variability and sophisticated text obfuscation techniques. Real-world attacks often include advance-fee scam narratives, counterfeit product advertisements, and fake corporate identities to establish false legitimacy.
attack_vectors: social engineering via crafted email narratives
malicious URLs leading to fraudulent websites
advertisement of counterfeit or illegal products

real_world_context.domain_insights: Phishing emails often contain suspicious URLs with uncommon or unrelated domain names, urgent or enticing subject lines promising financial or health benefits, and social engineering language soliciting personal or financial information. Attackers use obfuscated email addresses and encoded subject lines to evade detection. Multi-source datasets reveal attackers adapt tactics across different victim pools, increasing detection complexity.
real_world_context.attack_sophistication: Medium sophistication characterized by social engineering focus, leveraging text obfuscation, domain spoofing, and emotional manipulation but typically lacking advanced malware payloads.
real_world_context.technical_implementation: Attacks manifest as emails embedding URLs with uncommon TLDs, advance-fee scam narratives with long detailed stories, encoded or MIME-encoded subject lines, and insertion of nonsensical text blocks to confuse filters. Non-standard email addresses with irregular spacing or inserted characters are used to bypass simple pattern matching.
real_world_context.threat_landscape: These attacks represent a prevalent threat leveraging financial and health-related lures, widespread phishing campaigns across multiple sources, and increasing use of obfuscation and multi-lingual text to evade automated detection systems.
real_world_context.victim_impact: Victims risk financial loss, identity theft, exposure to counterfeit or illegal products, and compromised personal information due to successful social engineering and phishing attempts.

attack_signatures: phishing URL pattern: URLs with uncommon TLDs or unrelated domains (e.g., http://www.largevalue.net)
advance-fee scam narrative involving inheritance or abandoned funds
medication and health product spam with embedded URLs
fake corporate or banking identities with fraudulent contact details
encoded or MIME-encoded subject lines to evade keyword detection
insertion of unrelated or nonsensical text blocks
indicators_of_compromise: presence of suspicious URLs linking to newly registered or uncommon domains
short, enticing subject lines with monetary or urgent keywords
email body containing spelling/grammar errors and unusual formatting
generic greetings or alphanumeric codes in salutations
non-standard email address formatting with spaces or inserted characters
embedded contact information with suspicious email addresses or fax numbers
detection_criteria: flag emails with URLs from domains not in whitelist or registered within last 6 months
detect advance-fee scam keywords and phrases in body text
identify encoded subject lines and obfuscated email addresses
alert on combination of monetary promises in subject and embedded suspicious URLs
use NLP anomaly detection to find incoherent or nonsensical text blocks
normal_vs_malicious: benign emails have descriptive, relevant, and longer subject lines (5-15 words) vs. short, enticing phishing subjects (3-8 words)
benign URLs link to reputable domains without obfuscation vs. suspicious or uncommon domains in phishing
proper grammar and formatting in benign emails vs. errors and unusual formatting in malicious
standard email address syntax in benign vs. irregular spacing or inserted characters in malicious
presence of organizational disclaimers and signatures in benign emails absent in phishing
measurable_thresholds: flag emails with more than one suspicious indicator (e.g., suspicious URL + advance-fee keywords)
alert on URLs from domains registered within last 6 months
subject lines containing monetary amounts or urgent calls to action (e.g., '$2000/week')
body length thresholds: very short (<50 words) with promotional URLs or very long (>200 words) with scam narratives
mark emails with non-standard email address formatting as suspicious

attack_scenarios: An email with subject 'Claim your $2000/week now!' containing a URL to 'http://spreadreciprocity.com' and body text describing a quick financial opportunity with generic greeting and embedded suspicious contact email.
A long narrative email (>300 words) describing an inheritance claim requiring cooperation with bank officials, including advance-fee scam keywords and a suspicious URL with uncommon TLD.
A short promotional email advertising cheap medications with embedded obfuscated URLs and encoded subject line characters to evade keyword filters.
legitimate_scenarios: A corporate newsletter email with descriptive subject 'Q2 Financial Results and Upcoming Meetings' containing URLs linking to the official company domain and properly formatted contact details.
An academic call for papers email from a known conference source with structured information, standard email address formatting, and no suspicious URLs.
A technical discussion email with domain-specific jargon, coherent body text, and sender metadata consistent with known legitimate sources.

risk_reduction: Implement URL reputation filtering to block access to domains with poor or unknown reputation
Deploy machine learning models trained on multi-source phishing and benign email datasets to improve detection accuracy
Enforce sender authentication protocols such as SPF, DKIM, and DMARC to reduce email header spoofing
Use heuristic and signature-based detection to identify advance-fee scam narratives and encoded subject lines
Continuously monitor email subjects and bodies for emerging phishing lures and update detection rules accordingly

key_features_to_vary: subject line length and linguistic style
presence and type of URLs including domain TLDs
email body length and narrative complexity
email address formatting including obfuscation patterns
inclusion of encoded or MIME-encoded characters
pattern_preservation: phishing URL patterns with uncommon or unrelated domains
use of generic greetings or alphanumeric codes
insertion of nonsensical or unrelated text blocks
realism_requirements: maintain balanced classes with realistic proportions of phishing and benign emails
reflect multi-source linguistic diversity and formatting styles
simulate realistic email metadata consistent with source domains
preserve natural language errors and obfuscation tactics used in real attacks
diversity_dimensions: varied email sources and sender identities
range of subject and body lengths
multiple obfuscation techniques for email addresses and URLs
multi-lingual or poorly structured text inclusion
